title: Android Storage Still Full After Deleting Files? Why and What to Do
html:
Most of the time, deleted files are still on the phone in a Trash folder. Google Photos, Samsung Gallery and Files by Google each keep deleted items for 30 days. Empty the Trash, then clear app cache and data from the apps that use the most space. Your phone's Storage screen shows where the space is going.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026. Menus vary by brand.

I checked these screens on a vivo V23 Pro running Android 14 (Funtouch OS 14) on 11 Oct 2026. The phone showed 112 GB of 128 GB used before I touched anything.

1. Find out what is using the space

Open Settings, then Storage. Look at the categories. If an app or category is larger than you expect, start there. Google's help also separates storage (where you keep music and photos) from memory (where programs run), so a full storage screen has nothing to do with RAM.

2. Empty the Trash folders

  • Google Photos: Collections, then Trash. Google says items stay in Trash for 30 days before they are permanently deleted.
  • Samsung Gallery: menu, then Trash. Samsung keeps items for 30 days.
  • Files by Google: Menu, then Trash. Files stay for 30 days and are then deleted automatically.

To get the space back now, open the Trash and delete the items permanently. Be sure you do not need them: they cannot be restored afterwards. See how to recover deleted photos first if you are not sure.

3. Clear cache and data for the biggest apps

Go to Settings, then Apps, then See all apps, pick an app, then Storage and cache. Google describes the two buttons this way: clearing the cache deletes temporary data, and some apps may be slow the next time you open them; clearing storage permanently deletes all of the app's data. So clear the cache first, and clear storage only if you are sure you do not need what is inside.

4. Let Android do some of it

Settings, then Storage, then Free up space. Pick a category, tap Select files and move what you do not need to the Trash. In the menu under Settings, you can turn on Smart Storage, which clears backed-up photos and videos automatically when storage is nearly full. If you use Google Photos, check that your photos finished backing up before you delete the copies on the phone.

5. Remove apps you do not use

See our phone maintenance steps for Unused apps and Files by Google's Clean tab.

If the number still looks wrong

Some categories, such as System or Other, can be large and are hard to change. We could not find an official explanation of what they contain, so we do not guess.

On my vivo V23 Pro the RAM and storage screen lists System 34 GB, Apps 29 GB, Images 21 GB, Videos 17 GB, Audio 5.4 GB and Documents and others 4.3 GB. System was the biggest line, bigger than my Apps or photos. Tapping Manage storage on this screen takes you to options for removing files directly. In the Files by Google app, the Clean tab shows a Junk files card ("Unnecessary files taking up space") with a Clean button, and my Trash held 8.8 MB. I only opened these screens and did not tap Clean.

What to do next

  1. Open Settings, Storage, and look at what is biggest.
  2. Empty Trash in Photos, Gallery and Files.
  3. Clear cache for the largest apps, and remove apps you do not use.
